glossary.means: One private box per project. Your files, your agents, your terminals — nobody else's.
The program running inside a sandbox that owns the files and answers the editor.
One AI conversation doing one job. Several can run at once, each on its own copy of the code.
One round of an agent working: you ask, it acts, it reports.
A private copy of the code an isolated agent works in, so parallel agents cannot collide.
The strip of icons down the left of the editor. Space there is scarce and earned.
A package that adds screens, commands or agent tools without changing the core app.
Something you have connected — a GitHub account, a database, an API key.
A repo's own dev server, run by the sandbox and shown in a frame.
A description of what you want to exist. The deployment engine's input, not the product's.
The product you look at. Separate from the deployment engine, which is a bundled tool.
